name: TEST CLAUDE SKILL

chatHistory.content:
HOOK [0:00–0:30]
One of your 48 locations has been quietly bleeding orders for three weeks.
Brand-level reports won’t catch it, and the delivery platform dashboards won’t either.
An Apify, Zapier, and Power BI pipeline will — in about 15 minutes.
Here’s how.
[SCREEN: dashboard mockup, one location pulsing red on a map of the city]

BRIDGE [0:30–0:55]
Most competitive monitoring still needs someone to manually pull listings, location by location, and even then you’re only seeing one zip code on one day.
A system that runs itself doesn’t.
What we’re building today refreshes every location’s competitive position weekly, surfaces the ones that need attention, and stays out of your way the rest of the time.
Let’s get into it.
[SCREEN: cut to Apify Store, search bar]

ACTOR SETUP [0:55–2:00]
Head to Apify Store and find the E-commerce Scraping Tool.
Open it, click Create new Task — that saves the configuration for one specific location so we can reuse it on a schedule.
[SCREEN: Actor page → Create new Task button]
1. Search type: Food delivery options.
2. Delivery zone: postal code or coordinates for your first location.
3. Keyword: the product you sell. Let’s say it’s Doublecheese Burger.
The zone is the part that matters most.
The Actor benchmarks you against the competitors a real customer in that zone actually sees — not the brand average.
4. Scroll down and turn on Extended delivery review data.
That’s where the rating, pricing, and review signal comes from.
5. Save the Task. Run it once manually so you can check the output before any automation runs against bad config.
Then repeat — one Task per location.
[SCREEN: dataset preview showing one row of output]

EXPORTS [2:00–2:30]
Now, exports.
The output you want feeding Power BI is flat:
location identifier
delivery zone
own rating
competitor rating
price index
run date
These are the columns the dashboard slices on.
If one is missing here, you’ll have a permanent gap when you build the visuals.
Confirm them in the Apify dataset preview before moving on.
[SCREEN: Apify dataset preview, columns highlighted one by one]

ZAPIER WALKTHROUGH [2:30–4:30]
So, on to Zapier. Create a new Zap.
1. Trigger: Schedule by Zapier → Weekly.
Daily is overkill — competitor positioning doesn’t shift hour by hour, and weekly keeps the dashboard signal clean.
Pick whichever day works for your team’s review cycle.
2. Action: Apify → Run Actor.
Connect your Apify account with your API token.
Select the Task you saved for this first location.
Set Wait for finish = true.
This one matters — the next step needs the run complete before it pulls data. Without the flag, Zapier moves on too early and you end up with empty rows.
3. Action: Apify → Get Dataset Items.
Map the Dataset ID from step 2.
4. Action: Power BI → Add Rows to Dataset.
Map each field: location, zone, own rating, competitor rating, price index, date.
This is where the Apify output becomes the dashboard’s data, so map carefully — a wrong mapping here is invisible until someone notices the wrong location’s rating in a review meeting.
5. Test the Zap end-to-end. Confirm a row lands in Power BI.
6. To roll this across every location: duplicate the Zap, swap the Task in step 2 for each one.
[SCREEN: Zapier editor → each step appearing in sequence]

POWER BI [4:30–5:15]
Last piece, Power BI.
Open your workspace and confirm rows are arriving in the dataset every week.
Then build the visuals that actually drive decisions:
own ratings by location
competitor ratings per zone
price index comparison
sentiment trend over time
Add slicers for location, zone, date range, and platform — so the operations team can filter to the areas they manage and pricing can pull up just the markets they’re reviewing.
[SCREEN: finished Power BI dashboard, slicers highlighted]

OUTRO + CTA [5:15–5:45]
The next time one of your locations starts slipping, the dashboard catches it.
You see the trend before it lands in the monthly review — and you know whether it’s a competitor winning on value, a sentiment shift, or something operational, before it costs you the location.
To run your first scrape, create an Apify account from the link below. The Actor’s ready to go.
[SCREEN: Apify signup CTA, link in description callout]

That’s the full script in director’s-cut format. Read it aloud once and you’ll feel where to add or remo
